caseStudies.title: A 19-year-old monolith, brought to the latest Rails in six weeks
caseStudies.problem: Readytech's student management system: 1.71 million lines, 271 contributors, still on Rails 5.0 and Ruby 2.7. The goal was Rails 7.2, with 8.0 as a stretch.
caseStudies.approach: I led it with one other engineer and a fleet of parallel Claude and Codex agents, each fixing one file and its specs with backward-compatible changes. Those merged into the main branch continuously, while the next Rails version ran alongside, gated in CI.
caseStudies.result: Rails 8.1.3 on Ruby 4.0.5, skipping Ruby 3 entirely, and past the 8.0 stretch goal. Every production server was on 8.1 by July 20.

caseStudies.title: A two-minute dashboard, down to three seconds
caseStudies.problem: As founding engineer at a fintech startup, I found the largest client's dashboard taking about two minutes to load, or failing outright, on a codebase with no automated tests.
caseStudies.approach: Profiled with Skylight, AppSignal and PostHog, then rewrote the slow queries, moved heavy panels to async loading and right-sized the servers. Added containerised system tests from scratch.
caseStudies.result: Under three seconds, and test coverage from 0 to 25%+ in 48 days, while building bank reconciliation, Stripe payments and tax filing on state machines.
